evals.name: tof-distance-display
evals.prompt: This repo has a boring VL53L0X time-of-flight distance kit at src/kits/tof-distance that just prints millimeters. I want a new kit, src/kits/tof-distance-display, that makes it fun for 6th graders by putting the readings on a cheap round GC9A01 smartwatch display, wired the same way as src/kits/smartwatch-ref/config.py (that wiring is known to work). All I actually have is the sensor, a Pico, a breadboard and the display. No NeoPixels, no buzzer, nothing else. I can't test on hardware right now.
evals.expected_output: A verified-as-far-as-possible kit scaffold: a plan that separates confirmed from assumed hardware, resolves the I2C/SPI pin clash, a config.py with no duplicate pins, incremental labs that print TEST PASS including a Thonny Plotter lab and a sensor-free display hello lab, an upload script, a README, a lesson outline and box-cover brief that follow the guidelines, and an honest summary of what was and was not verified.
expectations: KIT-PLAN.md exists and is substantial
KIT-PLAN.md separates confirmed hardware from assumed hardware
KIT-PLAN.md compares at least two display options with prices
config.py has no duplicate GPIOs and valid bus pins (scripts/pin_check.py passes)
At least six numbered labs exist
Every lab imports config and hard-codes no pin numbers
At least four labs print TEST PASS
A Thonny Plotter lab exists and says it prints only numbers
A display hello lab exists that does not use the sensor
config.py does not import the display driver at the top level
upload-code.sh uploads lib, config and the labs with mpremote
upload-code.sh can install a chosen lab as main.py
The parent kit is untouched
README.md documents the expected TEST PASS output
SUMMARY.md says plainly that real hardware was not tested
SUMMARY.md says how the work was verified without hardware
The lesson outline has checkpoints, troubleshooting, teacher notes and the mascot rules
A box cover brief exists with a photo requirement, a QR code and at least 12 feature chips
No NeoPixel code was carried into the new kit
The display wiring matches the reference config (DC 4, CS 5, RST 6)
KIT-PLAN.md notices the GP2/GP3 pin clash between the parent's I2C and the display's SPI

evals.name: mic-level-display
evals.prompt: I have a MAX4466 microphone module (analog output on GP26) kit at src/kits/mic-level that only prints a loudness number. Make me a fun new kit for 6th graders, src/kits/mic-level-display, using a cheap 1.3 inch square 240x240 ST7789 SPI display (about $5 online). I don't have any wiring reference for that display, and I think it has a BL backlight pin but I'm honestly not sure. I also own one push button. Pico and breadboard as usual. I can't test on hardware right now.
evals.expected_output: A scaffold for an analog-sensor kit on a square display: valid ADC pin, planned SPI pins with no clash, unconfirmed hardware (BL pin) flagged rather than assumed, a plan that reads the button with an IRQ and a 50 ms debounce, no shouting contest, and the same lab ladder, docs and honesty as the first eval.
